# Processing Text Data

Terminal applications frequently process formatted text, logs, configuration files, and structured tables. Rust provides zero-cost slicing, streaming string buffers, and regular expressions to achieve peak throughput.

## Efficient In-Memory String Operations

Rust strings are valid UTF-8 byte sequences. Slicing on arbitrary byte indices can panic if it splits a multi-byte Unicode code point. Always prefer character or byte iterators:

```rust
fn tokenize_words(input: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    input
        .split_whitespace()
        .filter(|word| !word.is_empty())
        .collect()
}
```

## Reusable Buffers for High-Throughput Streaming

When processing gigabytes of text, allocating a new `String` for every line causes allocator bottlenecking. Reuse a single heap allocation with `BufRead::read_line`:

```rust
use std::io::{self, BufRead};

fn process_lines<R: BufRead>(mut reader: R) -> io::Result<usize> {
    let mut buffer = String::with_capacity(1024);
    let mut matching_lines = 0;

    while reader.read_line(&mut buffer)? > 0 {
        if buffer.contains("ERROR") {
            matching_lines += 1;
        }
        buffer.clear(); // Clears length while preserving allocated capacity
    }

    Ok(matching_lines)
}
```

## Pattern Matching with `regex`

When simple substring checks are insufficient, use the `regex` crate with pre-compiled regex engines:

```toml
[dependencies]
regex = "1.10"
```

```rust
use regex::Regex;

fn extract_ip_addresses(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    // Compile regex once (e.g. inside std::sync::LazyLock)
    let re = Regex::new(r"\b(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}\b").unwrap();

    re.find_iter(text)
        .map(|mat| mat.as_str())
        .collect()
}
```

## Streaming JSON with `serde_json`

Many modern CLIs emit or consume structured JSON streams (JSON lines / NDJSON). Use `serde_json::Deserializer::from_reader` to parse JSON records sequentially without loading the entire dataset into memory:

```rust
use serde::Deserialize;
use std::io::BufRead;

#[derive(Deserialize, Debug)]
struct LogRecord {
    timestamp: String,
    level: String,
    message: String,
}

fn parse_ndjson<R: BufRead>(reader: R) -> serde_json::Result<Vec<LogRecord>> {
    serde_json::Deserializer::from_reader(reader)
        .into_iter::<LogRecord>()
        .collect()
}
```
